published_prior_art.cite: AhnKasahara2026TransitionIndependence: Proposition 14 requires Assumption ID, whose positive-transition condition excludes a state absorbing for every type; HigginsJochmans2023MixturesDDC: common absorption for both types makes its full-rank condition fail.
DeanerKu2026DurationDiD studies aggregate binary absorbing-duration effects, not latent-type observational equivalence induced by initial absorber allocation.
BonhommeJochmansRobin2017Nonexchangeable supplies spectral-weight asymptotics; this is a model-specific analytic plug-in consequence once the new recovery map is established.

ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013GaussianBootstrap and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2015AntiConcentration supply the fixed-dimensional multiplier and singular-covariance ingredients; novelty is limited to their guarded-map integration.
Newey1990Efficiency gives the projection principle but not the tangent space, efficient score, or attainable bound for this absorbing latent-Markov face.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 14 identifies the latent parameter under RSM, M, and ID; ID(b) requires strictly positive relevant transition probabilities for every type and state sequence, excluding the shared absorbing-row face used here.

source_verification_receipts.version: 2023 author-hosted Journal of Econometrics article version
source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 10, Theorem 1; pp. 14–15, discussion of Assumption 1 and common absorption
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 identifies initial distributions, transition kernels, and type probabilities from four observations under Assumptions 1–3; the paper expressly notes that a state absorbing for both types makes Assumption 1 fail.

source_verification_receipts.version: author-accepted manuscript corresponding to Journal of Econometrics 201(2), 237–248
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs spectral/joint-diagonalization weights, estimates conditional moments by weighted averages, and derives the effect of whitening and diagonalization estimation on asymptotic behavior.
The paper gives Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration results permitting arbitrary covariance dependence while requiring positive coordinate variances for the relevant comparison bound.

The article establishes the semiparametric-efficiency framework used to calculate bounds and construct efficient estimators; it is a generic projection-method reference rather than a result for this Markov face.
The paper studies DiD identification and estimation for outcomes indicating arrival at an absorbing state through restrictions on group hazard rates.
The reconstruction setting requires at least twice as many observed states as latent chains; its spectral trail method therefore does not cover two active states with two latent types.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a short strict-containment corollary exhibiting an open parameter family with a common absorbing row that satisfies the active-minor assumptions while violating Ahn–Kasahara Assumption ID(b).

Promote the initial-absorption pair from one exact example to a generic non-identification proposition over an open family of baseline-exit allocations, while retaining nondegenerate active transitions.
For the efficiency OEQ, parameterize the constrained tangent space on the finite support and state a concrete normal-equations estimator candidate before solving the projection problem.

recommended_next_step: Advance the field-tier absorbing-face recovery package to Stage 0, retaining the exact witness and making strict separation from Ahn–Kasahara’s positivity condition explicit in the derivation.
